title: Reacting masses and yield practice sheet
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 37 (Reacting masses and yield practice sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 37: Reacting masses and percentage yield. To understand how to calculate reacting masses and percentage yield, and why yields are below 100%

model.title: 25.0 g of CaCO₃ is heated and 11.2 g of CaO is collected. Calculate the percentage yield. (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; Mr CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56)
An iron oxide contains 11.2 g of iron and 4.8 g of oxygen. Find its empirical formula. (Ar: Fe 56, O 16)

questions.q: Theoretical yield 25 g, actual 20 g. Percentage yield? [2 marks]
questions.model: Formula: % yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100. Substitute: 20 ÷ 25 × 100. Calculate: 80%.

questions.q: Give two reasons why yield is less than 100%.
questions.a: Reaction incomplete; product lost in transfer or filtering (also side reactions).

questions.q: Empirical formula of a compound with 2.4 g Mg and 1.6 g O?
Core: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. 50 g CaCO₃ is heated. Calculate the theoretical mass of CaO, then the % yield if 22.4 g is obtained.
questions.model: Teacher works the first step: moles CaCO₃ = 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 mol; ratio 1:1 so 0.5 mol CaO; mass = 0.5 × 56 = 28 g.

questions.q: Extend: 4.8 g of Mg burns to give 8.0 g of oxide. Find the empirical formula. [3 marks]
questions.a: Mass of O = 3.2 g (1); moles Mg = 4.8 ÷ 24 = 0.2, moles O = 3.2 ÷ 16 = 0.2 (1); ratio 1:1 so MgO (1).

questions.q: Stretch: In the metal oxide practical, why is the lid lifted from time to time?
questions.a: To let oxygen in so the magnesium can react, while stopping magnesium oxide smoke escaping.

questions.q: Big question: why do factories never get 100% of the expected product?
questions.a: Reactions may be incomplete, product is lost during separation and transfer, and side reactions make other products.
